title: oracle UPDATE with RETURNING fails if the column given is an expression, passes for INSERT
body:
as observed in #5812 

only oracle, only UPDATE

seems to have a different issue on SQL server for INSERT though.   will try to sidestep that one as it seems more driver related.

```diff

diff --git a/test/sql/test_returning.py b/test/sql/test_returning.py
index 9f2afd7b7..35aab075b 100644
--- a/test/sql/test_returning.py
+++ b/test/sql/test_returning.py
@@ -121,6 +121,7 @@ class ReturningTest(fixtures.TablesTest, AssertsExecutionResults):
             Column("persons", Integer),
             Column("full", Boolean),
             Column("goofy", GoofyType(50)),
+            Column("strval", String(50))
         )
 
     def test_column_targeting(self, connection):
@@ -197,6 +198,42 @@ class ReturningTest(fixtures.TablesTest, AssertsExecutionResults):
         )
         eq_(result2.fetchall(), [(1, True), (2, False)])
 
+    def test_insert_returning_w_expression(self, connection):
+        table = self.tables.tables
+        result = connection.execute(
+            table.insert().returning(table.c.strval + 'hi'),
+            {"persons": 5, "full": False, "strval": "str1"},
+        )
+
+        eq_(result.fetchall(), [('str1hi',)])
+
+        result2 = connection.execute(
+            select(table.c.id, table.c.strval).order_by(table.c.id)
+        )
+        eq_(result2.fetchall(), [(1, "str1")])
+
+    def test_update_returning_w_expression(self, connection):
+        table = self.tables.tables
+        connection.execute(
+            table.insert(),
+            [
+                {"persons": 5, "full": False, "strval": "str1"},
+                {"persons": 3, "full": False, "strval": "str2"},
+            ],
+        )
+
+        result = connection.execute(
+            table.update(table.c.persons > 4, dict(full=True)).returning(
+                table.c.strval + "hi"
+            )
+        )
+        eq_(result.fetchall(), [('str1hi',)])
+
+        result2 = connection.execute(
+            select(table.c.id, table.c.strval).order_by(table.c.id)
+        )
+        eq_(result2.fetchall(), [(1, "str1"), (2, "str2")])
+
     @testing.requires.full_returning
     def test_update_full_returning(self, connection):
         table = self.tables.tables

```
